purpose: StructFormer's OWN across-seed temporal-error variance on the M6 gate. The original margin used CNN spread as a stand-in because this had never been measured (KB Decisions 51, 55).
pre_commitment: Recorded BEFORE these runs: the recomputed margin is accepted in EITHER direction, including a harder bar. A transformer being less stable than a CNN was the stated expectation. It is, and M6 fails by more.
gate: guard-band pairs with >= 1.0 px median displacement — identical to m6_gate

comparison_to_cnn.note: StructFormer is LESS stable across seeds than the CNN; the corrected margin is wider.

recomputed_gate.reference: mean of the three Model C seeds, not attempt1's single draw (Decision 46)
recomputed_gate.model_d_te_source: read from m6_temporal_baseline.json -> m6_gate, not recomputed

decisive_observation: Model D lies INSIDE Model C's own seed range, and one Model C seed is BETTER than Model D. The improvement is not separable from StructFormer run-to-run noise. The earlier figure was measured against attempt1, a comparatively unlucky single draw.
known_difference_between_pooled_runs: attempt1 trained with train.num_workers=6; seedB/seedC with 2, reduced after a system OOM kill. Worker count does not enter the computation, so this should not affect results — but it is a difference between runs pooled into one sd, and is stated.
